result:
Implementation complete. Summary of the five owned files:

**`src/server/vision.ts`** (rewritten) — Pure inference extraction: `normalizePhoto()` (sharp, 32MP decode cap, EXIF-rotate, resize-inside-1600, JPEG q85), `analyzePhoto()` (768px vision crop, Ollama `qwen3-vl:4b-instruct` chat call with 240s timeout, native 0–1000 box→normalized-0–1 with `[0,0,1,1]` safe fallback + warning, zod `analysisSchema` validation, brand/size force-cleared), `isModelAvailable()` for readiness checks. `OLLAMA_URL` is a server-only env var, defaulting to `http://127.0.0.1:11434` (matching the existing hardcoded value — your condensed spec string didn't parse to a clean IP:port, so I trusted the code precedent over it).

**`src/server/analysisJobs.ts`** (new) — Owns the `worker_state` singleton (`CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`, created lazily here, never in database.ts). Exports `enqueueAnalysisJob`, `getAnalysisJobForOwner`, `cancelAnalysisJobForOwner`, `isWorkerHeartbeatRecent`, `cleanupOnStartup`, `acquireWorkerLock`/`renewWorkerLock`/`releaseWorkerLock`, and `runWorkerTick`. All DB work is parameterized SQL inside synchronous `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`/`COMMIT`/`ROLLBACK` blocks with zero `await` inside them. Quotas: 1 active job/user, 20 active globally, 20 accepted/user/day (UTC, `usage_daily`). Job lease 5 min, 2 attempts max, queued jobs expire in 1h, terminal jobs (with their photo/result) self-delete 1h after finishing. Completion writes are guarded by `status='running' AND lease_until=<claim value>` so a cancelled or re-claimed job can't be resurrected by a stale finish. The worker's own global lock reuses the same lease+heartbeat pattern, recoverable after 5 min if a worker dies.

**`scripts/analysis-worker.ts`** (new) — Thin process: `getReadyAuth()` + `cleanupOnStartup()` at boot, then a 2s poll loop calling `runWorkerTick` sequentially (inference is `await`ed in place, never detached), with a 10s heartbeat `setInterval` wrapped around each inference and cleared in `finally`. Stops only on SIGINT/SIGTERM; no control port; logs are static strings only.

**`src/app/api/analyze/route.ts`** (rewritten) — `GET`: auth-only, returns `{configured}` (model reachable AND worker heartbeat fresh). `POST`: `account(req,true)`, `readJson` 9MB, consent check, 6MB raster cap, canonicalizes via `normalizePhoto`, enqueues, returns 202 `{id,status:"queued"}`. All responses carry `privateHeaders`.

**`src/app/api/analysis-jobs/[id]/route.ts`** (new) — `GET` (owner read) returns `{id,status,result?}`/`{id,status,error}`, 404 for unknown/cross-user. `DELETE` (`account(req,true)`) cancels, clearing photo/result immediately even if running.

**Important correction I made against your prose spec:** I read the already-existing, root-owned `src/components/UploadDialog.tsx`, which already implements the client side of this exact queue (polling `/api/analysis-jobs/{id}`, deleting on cancel). It expects `GET /api/analyze` to return `{configured}` (not `{ready}`), and a completed job's `result` to be the **flat** `{items, warning, image}` shape, not `{analysis:{...}, image}`. I matched that real contract instead of my first draft.

**Limitations / things only root can verify:**
- No Bash tool was used or available; I have not run `tsc`, `eslint`, or the test suite — do not treat this as tested.
- `scripts/verify-vision.ts`, `verify-multiple.ts`, and `verify-empty-vision.ts` POST to `/api/analyze` unauthenticated and expect a synchronous body — they will now fail (401, then wrong shape even if auth were added) because `POST /api/analyze` is now an authenticated 202-queue endpoint. These are root-owned; they need rewriting to sign in, send `X-Style-Account`, and poll `/api/analysis-jobs/{id}` like `UploadDialog.tsx` already does. `debug-vision.ts` (hits Ollama directly) and `verify-browser-vision.ts` (drives the real UI) are likely unaffected or only mildly so.
- The old unauthenticated localhost-only Origin check and in-memory 10/min limiter are gone, superseded by the durable per-user/global/daily quotas — intentional, but a behavior change worth root's attention.
- `scripts/analysis-worker.ts` must actually be run as its own process for jobs to leave `queued` and for `configured` to ever be true; I didn't add an npm script since `package.json` is root-owned (suggest `"worker": "tsx scripts/analysis-worker.ts"`).
- Chosen constants (30s heartbeat freshness, 5 min job lease/worker-lock TTL, 1h queue/result TTL, 2 attempts, 1/20/20 quotas) come from your prose; worth a sanity check against desired UX.
